note: The Canadian funding map is its own world — no SNAP, no TEFAP. Federal and national programs fund food infrastructure, northern and Indigenous food access, and the national/provincial food-bank networks. For foundations, use the CRA charity search (the Canadian analog of the U.S. 990). Confirm current eligibility and guidelines before applying.

federal_channels.name: Local Food Infrastructure Fund (AAFC)
federal_channels.what: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada grants for community organizations to buy equipment and infrastructure — refrigeration, trucks, storage — that expands local food access. Built for exactly the kind of capacity a food bank needs to move more food.

federal_channels.name: Nutrition North Canada
federal_channels.what: Retail subsidy that lowers the cost of nutritious food in isolated northern communities. The backbone federal program for the North, where food costs and food insecurity are highest.

federal_channels.name: Nutrition North — Harvesters Support Grant
federal_channels.what: Funds Indigenous harvesting of traditional and country foods (hunting, fishing, gathering) in eligible communities — support on communities' own terms, and the closest Canadian analog to the U.S. FDPIR tribal food program. For northern and remote First Nations, Inuit and Métis communities, not urban centres.

federal_channels.name: Food Banks Canada
federal_channels.what: The national network — national food sourcing and sharing, disaster response, and grant programs its member food banks can access. Membership plugs a food bank into national purchasing and support.

federal_channels.name: Reaching Home (ESDC)
federal_channels.what: Canada's homelessness-strategy funding, delivered through community entities. Some food banks and their partners tap it for food-and-shelter programming that reaches the same households.

SK.name: Food Banks Saskatchewan
SK.what: The provincial association — provincial food sourcing, shared purchasing, and the channel through which recent Government of Saskatchewan food-bank funding flows. The first call for a Saskatchewan food bank.

SK.name: Government of Saskatchewan — community & social programs
SK.what: Provincial ministries (Social Services; Agriculture) periodically fund food security and community organizations. Check current provincial grant listings and recent food-bank commitments.

saskatoon.name: Saskatoon Community Foundation
saskatoon.what: Community foundation with $20.1M in annual revenue (FY2025) and an open, broad-eligibility grant program. Its Quality of Life Grants ($1,000–$10,000, one-year term) fund registered charities across Saskatoon with no cause restriction — a food bank is squarely eligible. CRA BN 119140911RR0001.

saskatoon.name: United Way of Saskatoon and Area
saskatoon.what: Mission explicitly includes "Moving People from Poverty to Possibility"; distributed roughly $2M/year in gifts to member agencies (FY2025). The most directly poverty-focused local funder for a Saskatoon food bank to approach. CRA BN 119276509RR0001.

calgary.name: The Calgary Foundation
calgary.what: Community foundation with $124.2M in annual revenue (FY2025) and five priority granting areas, the first of which is explicitly Reducing Poverty. A major, active, broad-eligibility grantmaker — a food bank fits squarely within its poverty-relief focus. CRA BN 108074436RR0001.

calgary.name: United Way of Calgary and Area
calgary.what: $56.3M in annual revenue (FY2024); its "Overcoming Poverty" priority area explicitly names helping people meet short-term basic needs like food and shelter as a first step toward stability. The most directly food-relevant local funder for a Calgary food bank to approach. CRA BN 130229750RR0001.

edmonton.name: Edmonton Community Foundation
edmonton.what: Community foundation with $160.9M in total revenue (FY2024, boosted by a large investment-gain year) and a broad, city-wide grant program supporting a vibrant, caring, healthy Edmonton — a food bank fits its general community-grant mandate. CRA BN 122437072RR0001.

edmonton.name: United Way of the Alberta Capital Region
edmonton.what: $25.5M in annual revenue (FY ending March 2025); explicitly targets "the root causes of poverty" and the most vulnerable in the community through mental wellbeing, education and financial-security programs. The most directly poverty-focused local funder for an Edmonton food bank to approach. CRA BN 119260487RR0001.

halifax.name: Community Foundation of Nova Scotia
halifax.what: Provincial community foundation headquartered in Halifax, with $8.5M in annual revenue (FY2024) and a broad, open grant program supporting communities across Nova Scotia. A food bank is squarely eligible under its general charitable-support mandate. CRA BN 870389368RR0001.

halifax.name: United Way Maritimes (United Way Halifax)
halifax.what: $13.0M in annual revenue (FY ending March 2026); explicitly funds programs for people experiencing poverty, including keeping people "housed, fed, safer and healthier." The most directly food-relevant local funder for a Halifax food bank to approach. CRA BN 119278232RR0001.

montreal.name: The Foundation of Greater Montreal
montreal.what: Community foundation with $79.3M in total revenue (FY2024) and grant programs spanning arts, education, social development, environment, sports and health — a food bank fits under its social-development granting. CRA BN 881979124RR0001.

montreal.name: Centraide du Grand Montréal
montreal.what: $88.5M in annual revenue (FY ending March 2025); mission explicitly supports vulnerable people and the organizations that help them. The most directly relevant local funder for a Montreal food bank to approach. CRA BN 118842517RR0001.

regina.name: Saskatchewan Community Foundation (South Saskatchewan Community Foundation)
regina.what: Community foundation headquartered in Regina, registered since 1969, with $46.2M in total revenue (FY2025). Broad mandate: grants and qualifying disbursements to support other charitable organizations, capacity building, and community giving — a food bank is squarely eligible under its general grantmaking. CRA BN 890271448RR0001.

regina.name: United Way of Regina
regina.what: $3.4M in annual revenue (FY ending June 2025); mission explicitly includes moving people from "Poverty to Possibility" as one of its 3 focus areas. The most directly poverty-focused local funder for a Regina food bank to approach. CRA BN 119278372RR0001.

toronto.name: Toronto Foundation
toronto.what: Toronto's community foundation, registered since 1981, with $68.6M in total revenue (FY2025). Mobilizes charitable funds and strategic granting to strengthen communities across Toronto — a food bank fits its general community-strengthening mandate. CRA BN 136491875RR0001.

toronto.name: United Way of Greater Toronto
toronto.what: $164.3M in annual revenue (FY ending March 2025); explicitly works to address the root causes of poverty across Peel, Toronto and York Regions. The most directly poverty-focused local funder for a Toronto-area food bank to approach. CRA BN 119278216RR0001.

vancouver.name: Vancouver Foundation
vancouver.what: Community foundation registered since 1967, with $256.6M in total revenue (FY2025). Broad grant programs (Neighbourhood Small Grants, Transforming Systems Grants, and more) fund charitable organizations across the region — a food bank is squarely eligible. CRA BN 119281640RR0001.

vancouver.name: United Way British Columbia
vancouver.what: $49.9M in annual revenue (FY ending March 2025); runs an explicit Food Security Initiative with 29 Regional Community Food Hubs helping British Columbians access nutritious food. The most directly food-relevant local funder for a Vancouver-area food bank to approach. CRA BN 108160185RR0001.

foundation_finder.label: Find Canadian foundations that fund food relief
foundation_finder.help: The Canada Revenue Agency's List of Charities is the open Canadian analog of the U.S. 990 — every registered charity and private/public foundation files an annual T3010 return. Search your city or province, filter to foundations, and open each one's return to see its giving and gauge fit before you apply.

order.label: Build a mixed truckload
order.help: Once the money's lined up, fill the trucks. Mix and match beans, lentils, chickpeas, oats, rice and grains to fill a 53-ft dry van — watch the load build to 26 pallets / 42,000 lb — then start a conversation with Food Aid Project, which sources and ships from Canada. Free planning tool, not a binding order.
